slides.title: SE(3)-Transformer
text: How to design attention layers using the steerable features?
Attention layers depend on non-linear pair-wise attention weights,
hence one needs to generate them in a non-equivariant way.
• Similar to tensor field network (TFN), apply non-linearities to scalar features.
• Different from TFN, generate scalar from a pair of steerable features.

slides.title: MACE: Higher Order Equivariant Message Passing
text: MACE: Higher Order Equivariant Message Passing
MACE proposes to use higher-order Clebsch-Gordan tensor product to expand the messages
in a hierarchical body order expansion.
• Sums run over neighbor of atom i.
• 𝒖+ is learnable message-passing function with correlation order 𝜈.
[Drautz, 2019] Atomic cluster expansion for accurate and transferable interatomic potentials

slides.title: MACE: Higher Order Equivariant Message Passing
text: MACE: Higher Order Equivariant Message Passing
In my wording, MACE consists of two types of layers.
In the first type of layer, it aggregates over the neighborhood using regular TFN updates.
In the second type of layer, it performs high-order CG tensor product between
node-wise features without aggregation (similar to 1x1 convolution).
CG tensor product                 High-order CG tensor product

slides.title: End of Section
text: • [Finzi et al., 2020] Generalizing Convolutional Neural Networks for Equivariance to Lie Groups on
(LieConv, provides a view of gemetricGNN as generalizing convolution to Lie groups)
• [Geiger and Smidt, 2022] e3nn: Euclidean Neural Networks
(e3nn, a very general framework for building E(3) equivariant trainable functions )
• [Musaelian et al., 2022] Learning local equivariant representations for large-scale atomistic dynamics
(Allegro, learning message representation of second-order message passing similar to MACE)
• [Batatia et al., 2022] The Design Space of E(3)-Equivariant Atom-Centered Interatomic Potentials
(BOTNet, general framework for ACE-based body-ordered tensor network)

slides.title: End of Section
text: • [Zitnick et al., 2022] Spherical Channels for Modeling Atomic Interactions
(SCN, predecessor of eSCN which is non-equivariant for faster computation)
• [Le et al., 2022] Equivariant Graph Attention Networks for Molecular Property Prediction
(EQGAT, attention-based geometric GNN similar to SE(3)-Transformer and Equiformers)
• [Thölke et al., 2022] Equivariant Transformers for Neural Network based Molecular Potentials
(ET, transformer-based geometric GNN similar to SE(3)-Transformer and Equiformers)
